title: Group-count and area-concentration controls retain the Cycle 25 radio excess in matched area models
abstract: We test whether whole-group number and area concentration explain the Cycle 25 emission rise at fixed dark area. Common-day monthly models in January 2011 to November 2013 and January 2022 to November 2024 retain a 10.42% F10.7 rise after group-count and effective-group controls at fixed HMI area. The area-only estimate is 9.92%. Ground-area models retain a rise of about 12.6%. Mg II also retains a positive offset. Nonlinear, phase, source and joint-support checks test the fitted explanation. The shared-support sample has few late months. These results constrain a simple whole-group redistribution model under stable measurement scales; they do not identify solar physics or exclude all changes in group structure. We provide code, aggregate estimates, a figure, exact source hashes and external-data retrieval instructions. External observations and derived databases remain outside the baseline bundle.

display.caption: Fitted Cycle 25 changes in total F10.7 at fixed area with added group controls. Bars show conditional 95% residual-block intervals. The joint-support check has only six or eight late months.
